newsitem.title: USA: R.R. Donnelley, Stream to take unit public.
newsitem.headline: R.R. Donnelley, Stream to take unit public.

text.p: R.R. Donnelley & Sons Co and Stream International Inc, which is about 80 percent owned by Donnelley, said they intend to take Stream's Outsource Technical Support business public.

This business provides technical support services to software publishers and hardware manufacturers worldwide. A registration statement relating to the offering is expected to be filed in the first quarter of 1997.
R.R. Donnelley said it is strategically realigning its businesses to focus on its base, print-related services.

The company said it is working with Stream to evaluate alternatives to maximize the value of its investment in Stream's other two businesses, Corporate Technologies and Outsource Manufacturing Services, but no transactions have been determined.
An initial public offering, sale to a strategic investor or a Stream management buyout all are possible, it said.
Stream International, with 1995 sales of $1.6 billion, was formed in April 1995 through the merger of R.R. Donnelley's Global Software Services business unit and Corporate Software Inc.

Stream chief executive officer Terry Leahy said his company will continue to invest in Corporate Technologies and Outsource Manufacturing Services."Both are well positioned to continue to provide the differentiated value and service that customers have grown to expect over the past decade," he said in a statement.
Stream provides PC-based software and management services to the vendor and corporate marketplaces.
R.R. Donnelley provides printing and digital information services.
